## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Paṭhamabodhi Sutta* (Ud 1.1; PTS Ud 1) is the opening discourse of the *Bodhivagga* in the *Udāna* of the Khuddaka Nikāya. It depicts the Buddha, immediately after his enlightenment under the Bodhi tree, contemplating specific conditionality (*idappaccayatā*) and dependent arising (*paṭiccasamuppāda*) in forward order. Through this insight, the Buddha crystallizes the understanding that all experience arises conditioned by causes, fundamentally denying the existence of an unchanging essence or soul (*ātman*) [Runehov and Oviedo 2013]. The text is cited in early post-canonical exegetical works, including the *Nettippakaraṇa* (Ne 37) and the *Kathāvatthu* (Kv 2.3).
